title: Backcasting from 'Watermarks Survive in the Wild': Robustness-Testing a Public Text Watermark

original_idea.body:
# Backcasting from 'Watermarks Survive in the Wild': Robustness-Testing a Public Text Watermark

**Problem:** A success state for content-provenance governance requires that AI-text watermarks survive realistic adversarial handling (paraphrase, translation, light editing). If watermarks break trivially, provenance-based policy mechanisms collapse.

**Direction:** Use an open-source text-watermarking implementation on a small open model to generate watermarked text, then apply a battery of realistic transformations (synonym swap, back-translation, sentence reordering, manual edits) and measure how watermark-detection accuracy degrades with each. Report a robustness curve and the point at which detection becomes unreliable.

**Why it matters:** Backcasting from 'provenance policy works' shows watermark robustness as the precondition. A concrete robustness-degradation study tells policymakers how much weight watermarking can bear before it fails — relevant to EU AI Act transparency obligations. Needs only a small open model and CPU/GPU text processing; no proprietary tooling.

**Relevant context:** EU AI Act and GPAI Code transparency obligations touch on AI-content marking; open watermarking schemes (e.g., KGW-style) have public implementations; Open Problems in Technical AI Governance lists provenance/verification among capacities.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain to provenance policy but watermarking is more misuse/misinfo-adjacent than core catastrophic-risk; a gap in the chain.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Using an open watermarking implementation and applying transformations; guided, single GPU.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped robustness-curve experiment with clear degradation metrics.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public tooling and open models; independent robustness study labs deprioritize.

low_compute.reasoning: Small open model plus text transforms, single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Text-watermark robustness against paraphrase/translation is a well-studied area.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Watermark robustness against paraphrase/translation attacks is well-studied.
